column1: # Changes to the Hebrew speaker layer from the review pass over doubtful passages (shoresh/macula/speaker_review.py; applied last by
# build_speaker_layer.py, left out with --no-review). Each row: the word key it is keyed on, the field (speaker, first, last, drop:
# a quotation found by its first word; add: a new quotation from first to last inside parent; level: the level of the segments
# first..last; frame: the chapter's frame), the value, the reason the Hebrew gives, and its source (the reviewers and the prompt).

column4: reason
כֹּה תֹאמַר אֲלֵהֶם tells Rehoboam what to say; 'I' in קָטָנִּי עָבָה מִמָּתְנֵי אָבִי and וַאֲנִי אֹסִיף is Rehoboam. The bounds (10:10b to the end of 10:11) are right. [layout-02]
כֹּה־תֹאמַר לָעָם follows the young men's inquit לֵאמֹר and opens their own speech; it is not a separate speech. [layout-02]
The young men's speech begins right after לֵאמֹר with כֹּה־תֹאמַר לָעָם; the relative אֲשֶׁר־דִּבְּרוּ אֵלֶיךָ cannot start it. [layout-02]

God's words after גַּם־בִּי הִתְאַנַּף יְהוָה … לֵאמֹר run without a new inquit through 1:40 (וְלָהֶם אֶתְּנֶנָּה, God's first person; וְאַתֶּם פְּנוּ לָכֶם וּסְעוּ); 1:41 returns to Moses' narration with וַתַּעֲנוּ. [layout-03]
1:39-40 continue the same divine speech at the same level with no new inquit; merged into L00059.4. [layout-03]
The inquit is וַיִּקְצֹף וַיִּשָּׁבַע לֵאמֹר with יְהוָה as subject (1:34), and 'I' in נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי and וְלוֹ־אֶתֵּן is God. [layout-03]
וַתַּעֲנוּ וַתֹּאמְרוּ אֵלַי: the Israelites Moses addresses speak to him (חָטָאנוּ לַיהוָה, אֲנַחְנוּ נַעֲלֶה). [layout-03]
Their words end with אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּנוּ יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ; וַתַּחְגְּרוּ … וַתָּהִינוּ לַעֲלֹת הָהָרָה is Moses' narration again (second plural wayyiqtol). [layout-03]

הוּא רָשָׁע בַּעֲוֺנוֹ יָמוּת וְדָמוֹ מִיָּדְךָ אֲבַקֵּשׁ is God's own continued speech to Ezekiel (the consequence clause; 'your hand' = Ezekiel, 'I will require' = God), parallel to הוּא בַּעֲוֺנוֹ יָמוּת in 3:19 and וְדָמוֹ מִיָּדְךָ אֲבַקֵּשׁ in 3:20, which are level 1. No inquit; not a quotation. [layout-04]
The inquit is בְּאָמְרִי לָרָשָׁע: 'when I say to the wicked', so the speaker of מוֹת תָּמוּת is God ('I'), not the one addressed. [layout-04]

God's speech to Ezekiel (בֶּן־אָדָם הִנָּבֵא … וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵיהֶם) does not stop at 34:6: 34:7 לָכֵן רֹעִים שִׁמְעוּ אֶת־דְּבַר יְהוָה continues the prophecy Ezekiel is told to speak, and 34:8 resumes God's first person (חַי־אָנִי, צֹאנִי). It should run on as far as the oracle does; 34:8 is the end of this passage. [layout-05]

Ezekiel's message to the shepherds continues with his own call לָכֵן רֹעִים שִׁמְעוּ אֶת־דְּבַר יְהוָה (YHWH in the third person, so the messenger's words at level 2) and the divine words it announces; it is not the level-0 frame. [layout-05]
q04798 puts 34:8 at level 1 directly in the frame; these are God's words inside Ezekiel's message (replaced by the added quotation). [layout-05]
חַי־אָנִי נְאֻם אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה … צֹאנִי, רֹעַי: God's first-person oath announced by שִׁמְעוּ אֶת־דְּבַר יְהוָה inside Ezekiel's message; level 3, continuing past 34:8 with the oracle. [layout-05]
פֶּן־יַסִּית אֶתְכֶם חִזְקִיָּהוּ לֵאמֹר יְהוָה יַצִּילֵנוּ: after the inquit, Hezekiah's words (נוּ = 'us') are a quotation inside the king's words (level 3), like 36:15. [layout-06]

q03413.t274 gives 36:17-19 to Hezekiah, but 'I' there is the Assyrian king (בֹּאִי, וְלָקַחְתִּי, מִיָּדִי) and Hezekiah is spoken of in the third person (פֶּן־יַסִּית אֶתְכֶם חִזְקִיָּהוּ); merged into the king's quotation. [layout-06]
q03413.4 (36:20, no speaker) is the end of the same royal speech (מִיָּדִי); merged into the king's quotation. [layout-06]
The king's words after כִּי כֹה אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר run without a new inquit through 36:20: first person of the king עַד־בֹּאִי וְלָקַחְתִּי אֶתְכֶם (36:17), מִיָּדִי (36:19, 20). [layout-06]

q03413.1 is a real quotation (after Rabshakeh's messenger formula כֹּה אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ) but has no speaker; the words אַל־יַשִּׁא לָכֶם חִזְקִיָּהוּ are the king's, one level under Rabshakeh. Its extent (36:14b-16a, with Hezekiah's words in 36:15 one level deeper) is right. [layout-06]
כִּי־כֹה אָמַר יְהוָה opening the oracle is the prophet's messenger formula (Jeremiah's frame); God's words begin after it. [layout-07]

God's speech runs on through 30:10 with no change of speaker: מַדּוּעַ רָאִיתִי (30:6, God's 'I'), the formulas נְאֻם יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת (30:8) and נְאֻם־יְהוָה (30:10) inside it, אֶשְׁבֹּר … אֲנַתֵּק (30:8), אֲשֶׁר אָקִים לָהֶם (30:9), עַבְדִּי יַעֲקֹב (30:10). The end given is the end of W00328 as the table has it; the speech may continue past the passage. [layout-07]
קוֹל חֲרָדָה שָׁמָעְנוּ is first plural ('we heard'): God cites the people's cry; the 'we' is not God. [layout-07]
The cry is קוֹל חֲרָדָה שָׁמָעְנוּ פַּחַד וְאֵין שָׁלוֹם; God's own voice resumes with the imperatives שַׁאֲלוּ־נָא וּרְאוּ (30:6). [layout-07]
There is no inquit for Jeremiah; 'I' in מַדּוּעַ רָאִיתִי continues God's speech after כֹּה אָמַר יְהוָה, so 30:5b-6 is not a Jeremiah quotation. [layout-07]
W00327 (30:5b-7, הוֹי כִּי גָדוֹל הַיּוֹם הַהוּא) is a fragment of the same divine speech; merged into q03963. [layout-07]
וְהָיָה בַיּוֹם הַהוּא נְאֻם יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת followed by God's first person אֶשְׁבֹּר is a formula inside God's words, not a Jeremiah quotation. [layout-07]
W00328 (30:8-10) continues the same divine speech (אֶשְׁבֹּר, אָקִים, עַבְדִּי יַעֲקֹב); merged into q03963. [layout-07]

The message does not stop before וָאֶתֵּן אֹתָם לְאַהֲרֹן (7:34b): it is the second half of the same sentence as לָקַחְתִּי (same speaker 'I', same object). 7:35 זֹאת מִשְׁחַת אַהֲרֹן is the narrator's summary. [layout-08]

דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר: the law that follows is the message Moses is told to say to the Israelites (second plural תִּתְּנוּ, שַׁלְמֵיכֶם in 7:32 addresses them), so by convention 7 it is a quotation inside God's command whose speaker is Moses. [layout-08]
Solomon quotes the first woman: זֹאת אֹמֶרֶת זֶה־בְּנִי הַחַי וּבְנֵךְ הַמֵּת ('my son … your son', the woman's 'I'); a level-2 quotation inside the king's speech. [notes-01]
וְזֹאת אֹמֶרֶת introduces the second woman's words לֹא כִי בְּנֵךְ הַמֵּת וּבְנִי הֶחָי; a second level-2 quotation in Solomon's speech, ending with the verse. [notes-01]
After וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ the king's words begin with זֹאת אֹמֶרֶת ('this one says'); that participial inquit is part of Solomon's speech, not narrative. [notes-01]

אִם־כֹּה יֹאמַר טוֹב: the subject of יֹאמַר is 'your father' (אָבִיךָ, 20:6), and כֹּה points to his words, which are just טוֹב; שָׁלוֹם לְעַבְדֶּךָ is David's own conclusion. A one-word level-2 quotation by Saul. Note: it starts inside segment 8733 (after the inquit אִם־כֹּה יֹאמַר), so the segment must be split at 090200070041. [notes-02]
וְאָמַרְתָּ: David tells Jonathan what to say to Saul (נִשְׁאֹל נִשְׁאַל מִמֶּנִּי דָוִד, I = Jonathan); naming him is clearer than '(the one addressed)'. [notes-02]

אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה בֹּטֵחַ בּוֹ לֵאמֹר לֹא תִנָּתֵן יְרוּשָׁלִַם בְּיַד מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר: after לֵאמֹר, the words attributed to Hezekiah's God are quoted directly; one level deeper (level 3). [notes-03]
The king's instruction contains the whole message to be delivered; it ends with 19:13, before the narrative וַיִּקַּח חִזְקִיָּהוּ אֶת־הַסְּפָרִים (19:14). [notes-03]
The message is one level under the king's instruction כֹּה תֹאמְרוּן … לֵאמֹר. [notes-03]

19:9 וַיִּשְׁלַח מַלְאָכִים אֶל־חִזְקִיָּהוּ לֵאמֹר: the sender, the king of Assyria, says כֹּה תֹאמְרוּן אֶל־חִזְקִיָּהוּ to his messengers (second plural); the speaker is the king, not '(he/she)'. [notes-03]

אַל־יַשִּׁאֲךָ אֱלֹהֶיךָ … is the message the messengers (subject of תֹאמְרוּן) are to say; it is not Rabshakeh (he is not in this embassy). The first person אֲבוֹתַי (19:12) is the king's, carried inside the message. [notes-03]

כִּי־יִשְׁאָלְךָ בִנְךָ מָחָר לֵאמֹר introduces the son's direct question מָה הָעֵדֹת וְהַחֻקִּים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִים אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֶתְכֶם ('our God', 'you' plural): a quotation one level inside the speech, parallel to the answer L00063.1. [notes-04]

The father's answer continues in the first plural through 6:24-25 (וַיְצַוֵּנוּ יְהוָה, לְטוֹב לָנוּ, וּצְדָקָה תִּהְיֶה־לָּנוּ כִּי־נִשְׁמֹר … כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּנוּ); the second-singular address to Israel returns only at 7:1 (כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ). [notes-04]

From 6:1 on YHWH is spoken of in the third person (כִּי אֵל קַנָּא יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ, אֲשֶׁר צִוָּךְ, כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהוָה, כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ): Moses addressing Israel, not God. God's reply at Sinai (5:28b-31, after וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֵלַי) is the only divine speech here and should be split off as a God quotation one level deeper inside Moses' speech; its keys lie before this passage. [notes-04]
Moses' speech to Aaron (וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל־אַהֲרֹן) is אֱמֹר אֶל־כָּל־עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל plus the message, to the end of 16:9; 16:10 is narration. [notes-05]
q00637 puts the message at level 1 beside Moses' command; it belongs one level under it (added below). [notes-05]
קִרְבוּ לִפְנֵי יְהוָה כִּי שָׁמַע אֵת תְּלֻנֹּתֵיכֶם is what Aaron is told to say (אֱמֹר, second singular to Aaron); level 2, speaker Aaron, who delivers it in 16:10 (כְּדַבֵּר אַהֲרֹן). [notes-05]
Pharaoh's speech to Joseph (וַיֹּאמֶר פַּרְעֹה אֶל־יוֹסֵף) runs from אֱמֹר אֶל־אַחֶיךָ to the end of 45:20 and contains the messages. [notes-06]
q00456 keeps the messages at level 1 and runs over וְאַתָּה צֻוֵּיתָה, which is Pharaoh addressing Joseph again (second singular); replaced by the two messages added below. [notes-06]
אֱמֹר אֶל־אַחֶיךָ: זֹאת עֲשׂוּ טַעֲנוּ … וְאִכְלוּ אֶת־חֵלֶב הָאָרֶץ (second plural to the brothers) is the message Joseph is to deliver; level 2. [notes-06]

וְאַתָּה צֻוֵּיתָה (Pharaoh to Joseph, level 1) introduces a second message for Joseph to say: זֹאת עֲשׂוּ קְחוּ־לָכֶם … וּנְשָׂאתֶם אֶת־אֲבִיכֶם וּבָאתֶם, וְעֵינְכֶם אַל־תָּחֹס … לָכֶם הוּא (second plural to the brothers); level 2 through 45:20. [notes-06]

וְגַם אָמַרְתִּי is an inquit (first-person qatal of אמר) followed by direct first-person speech לֹא־אֲגָרֵשׁ אוֹתָם מִפְּנֵיכֶם וְהָיוּ לָכֶם לְצִדִּים …, exactly like וָאֹמַר + לֹא־אָפֵר בְּרִיתִי in 2:1; a level-2 quotation by the same speaker, ending with 2:3. [notes-07]
q01353.t119 (no speaker) is the continuation of q01353.i72; merged into it. [notes-07]

The words quoted after וָאֹמַר continue into 2:2: וְאַתֶּם לֹא־תִכְרְתוּ בְרִית … מִזְבְּחוֹתֵיהֶם תִּתֹּצוּן is the second half of the same former command; the angel's present reproach resumes with וְלֹא־שְׁמַעְתֶּם בְּקֹלִי. [notes-07]
וָאֶתֵּן אֹתָם לְאַהֲרֹן (7:34b) completes the sentence begun with לָקַחְתִּי in the message; the message ends with 7:34. See also layout-08. [notes-08]
דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר (7:23): the law כָּל־חֵלֶב … לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ is what Moses is to say to the Israelites; name him rather than '(the one addressed)'. [notes-08]
Same structure in 7:29 (דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר); the message's speaker is Moses (it has none now). See also layout-08. [notes-08]

God's oracles end with נְאֻם־יְהוָה (2:16). 3:1 שִׁמְעוּ אֶת־הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהוָה עֲלֵיכֶם is the prophet's summons (YHWH in the third person) ending in the inquit לֵאמֹר, and 3:3-5 (הֲיֵלְכוּ שְׁנַיִם יַחְדָּו, הֲיִשְׁאַג אַרְיֵה) are rhetorical questions with no divine first person or formula, leading to 3:7-8 where the prophet speaks of God in the third person. [oracle-01]
After the inquit לֵאמֹר (3:1) God speaks in the first person: רַק אֶתְכֶם יָדַעְתִּי … עַל־כֵּן אֶפְקֹד עֲלֵיכֶם; this alone is the word announced. [oracle-01]

וְאָמַרְתִּי לְלֹא־עַמִּי is first singular with God as 'I', continuing God's speech of 2:16-25 (וּזְרַעְתִּיהָ לִּי, וְרִחַמְתִּי); it is not the prophet's frame. W00095 should start here at least, and join the divine speech before it. [oracle-02]
עַמִּי־אַתָּה is what God ('I' of וְאָמַרְתִּי) says to Lo-ammi; 'my people' is God's word, not the people's. [oracle-02]
God's words to Lo-ammi are only עַמִּי־אַתָּה; וְהוּא יֹאמַר is God's own narration introducing the answer, back at level 1. [oracle-02]
After וְהוּא יֹאמַר the people ('he' = Lo-ammi) answer אֱלֹהָי, 'my God': their words, one level inside God's speech. [oracle-02]
God's command (עוֹד לֵךְ אֱהַב־אִשָּׁה …) ends with 3:1; וָאֶכְּרֶהָ לִּי (3:2) is Hosea's first-person narration of carrying it out, not God's speech. [oracle-02]

וָאֹמַר אֵלֶיהָ: Hosea (the narrator's 'I') speaks to the woman: יָמִים רַבִּים תֵּשְׁבִי לִי … וְגַם־אֲנִי אֵלָיִךְ (second feminine singular to her). 3:4 כִּי יָמִים רַבִּים יֵשְׁבוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל turns to Israel in the third person and is the narrator's explanation. [oracle-02]
Hosea 3 is told by Hosea in the first person from its first line (וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֵלַי, וָאֶכְּרֶהָ לִּי, וָאֹמַר); the chapter's frame is empty in its first segments. [oracle-02]

God's announced word ends with the closing formula נְאֻם־יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (17:6). 17:7-9 has no formula and no divine first person and speaks of God in the third person (יִשְׁעֶה הָאָדָם עַל־עֹשֵׂהוּ, אֶל־קְדוֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל): Isaiah's own voice in the frame. [oracle-03]
הָאֹמֵר לְךָ is part of God's own sentence כִּי אֲנִי יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מַחֲזִיק יְמִינֶךָ הָאֹמֵר לְךָ (God's first person, as in 41:8-13a); it is not frame narrative at level 0. [oracle-04]

אַל־תִּירָא אֲנִי עֲזַרְתִּיךָ is what God (the subject of הָאֹמֵר) says, quoted inside God's speech; W00194's speaker (God) and extent are right, but it sits one level under God's speech of 41:8-13. [oracle-04]
